correctness.rationale: Checked the actual Higashine theorem: A_t corresponds to b^q=t, B_c ranges over all k, D_d over K, and the group types match. P is uniquely infinitely incident; any other plane contains at most three lines, from the conic of B directions and the pencil of D lines. The q² dual points on a smooth conic force conic preservation by Bézout; three K-points then force a K-rational Möbius map, with ∞ fixed as the missing K-point. The projectivity on H is uniquely determined by the conic action (four conic points form a frame). In the extension off H the B_c identity forces δ=a² and w=v²/a². Direct substitution gives all three claimed permutations, so the group is exact, with additive two-dimensional kernel and the finite affine section. Norm-one is necessary and sufficient to preserve the nonzero D label partition. Translations give C_{L_q(u),v}; surjectivity and coefficient comparison prove distinctness in (s,t), not in (u,v). Each s has q/2 preimages, already stated in the original. Projective conjugation preserves projection group isomorphism types. The statement is on geometric lines/reduced group, not the nonreduced stabilizer scheme.
